doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Building the big band and township keyboards and Zulu guitar
summary: In 1982 he started a university big band as the core of a program; keyboards and Zulu guitar traditions explained.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well this is getting quite technical but when I started — by the way I don’t come from a big band background so I was learning on the job. But one of the things I knew — it’s no longer true but we’re back in 1982 and I thought the only absolute basis for having a university jazz program is you have to have a big band because you’re going to pull in some people from the community, you’ll pull in people from other departments who might have learned instruments, they might be on university staff or they might be medical students or whatever they are, but you create a core and that’s the beginning of a culture and a network that you won’t get if you’re just going to get five jazz pianists and a singer and a guitar player. You know the first step really is to, you know, is to create the big band and so I had to do something that I’d never done before. And so all of these things came to the surface but now I’m remembering more directly what your question is.

Yeah, keyboards because churches have pianos. Guitars because at least in Natal there is a very strong Zulu guitar tradition. And yes they do use different tunings and it’s no more like classical guitar than flamenco guitar is like classical guitar. It’s its own thing — virtuosic solo music. You don’t really get guitar bands. You get a front guy who is the star, is the guitar player.
